info.description:
Adapter that answers the Rotector custom API contract from the SCSN and RAB
services.

Configure the Rotector extension with these URLs, replacing the host:

* SCSN single lookup: `https://your-host/v1/scsn/v1/lookup/user/{userId}`
* SCSN batch lookup:  `https://your-host/v1/scsn/v1/lookup/users`
* RAB single lookup:  `https://your-host/v1/rab/v1/lookup/user/{userId}`
* RAB batch lookup:   `https://your-host/v1/rab/v1/lookup/users`

All endpoints require an API key, issued in `Keys/Consumers.json` and accepted via
`X-Auth-Token`, `Authorization: Bearer` or a bare `Authorization` value. Both URL
schemes must be served over HTTPS. Handled errors are returned with HTTP 200 and a
{"success": false, "error": "..."} body, as the extension treats any other status
code as a failure.

A consumer can discover what its own key allows at `GET /v1/whoami`, and read its own
usage at `GET /v1/usage`.
info.summary: SCSN and RAB user flag lookups for the Rotector extension.
info.title: RoProtect - Rotector custom API

post.description:
Returns avatar CDN URLs and names for multiple Discord users.

Name fields follow the single endpoint: `username`, `globalName` and the resolved `displayName`.

The response is a flat map keyed by stringified Discord user ID. Users Discord does not know (404) are omitted from the map. If all requested users are unknown, an empty map is returned.

Non-numeric entries in `ids` are skipped rather than failing the whole batch, so one bad entry cannot cost you the other lookups.

No {success, data} wrapper; the body is the map itself.

get.description:
Returns the avatar CDN URL and the user's name for one Discord user.

`username` is the login handle, `globalName` the display name they chose (null when unset), and `displayName` is the one to render, already resolved to `globalName` or `username`.

If the user has no custom avatar, `avatarUrl` and `avatarHash` are null and `isAnimated` is false. If Discord does not know the user at all, every name and avatar field is null and only `userId` is set.

The endpoint returns the bare avatar object (not the {success, data} wrapper) so it validates directly against DiscordAvatar schema. A handled failure returns the failure wrapper at HTTP 401/403/400/503.

get.description:
Returns a verdict on one Roblox group. The body is the verdict itself, not the `{success, data}` wrapper the user routes use, because the extension validates it against a fixed group schema.

`flagType` uses the narrower group set: `-1` unknown, `0` safe, `1` pending, `2` unsafe, `3` queued, `5` mixed, `6` past offender. `4` and `8` are user-only and are never returned here.

A group SCSN does not track is reported as `-1` rather than `0`: SCSN only holds records for groups somebody registered for monitoring, so its silence is not evidence the group is safe. A group still being processed is `3`. A group tagged NP, which SCSN has no permission to read, is `5`.

schema.description: The verdict on one group. Unknown values must be sent as ``-1``.

flagType.description: Group verdict. `-1` = unknown (SCSN holds no data on this group, or the record is incomplete) | `0` = safe | `1` = pending | `2` = unsafe | `3` = queued, still processing | `5` = mixed, evidence inconclusive | `6` = past offender. `4` and `8` are user-only and are not valid here; any unrecognised value is read as `-1`.
flagType.title: Flagtype

reasons.title: Reasons

200.description: The verdict on one group. Unknown values must be sent as ``-1``.

get.description:
One page of the members SCSN tracks in a group. SCSN has no batch variant of this route: paginate it with `cursor`.

`limit` defaults to 24 and is clamped to 100. `cursor` is opaque - echo back the `nextCursor` you were given, and omit it for the first page. `active` is a string, `"true"` or `"false"`, and filters by whether the member is still in the group; any other value is ignored.

`totalCount` counts every member matching the filter, not just this page. `nextCursor` is always present and is null on the last page, where `hasMore` is false.

SCSN exposes no display name or headshot for a member, so `displayName` falls back to the username and `thumbnailUrl` is null. Both keys are always present.
get.summary: Tracked members of an SCSN group

get.description:
Looks up SCSN group-membership records for one Roblox user.

Active membership in an SCSN-tracked group is reported as `flagType` 2 (Confirmed). Groups the user has since left are listed separately and downgrade the result to `flagType` 6 (Past offender) when no active membership remains. A user with no SCSN record at all is returned as `flagType` 0 (Unflagged). The content category is inferred from the tracked group names and omitted when nothing matches.

get.description:
Looks up The All Seeing Eye (TASE) records for one Roblox user.

TASE indexes Discord accounts rather than Roblox accounts, so the Roblox user ID is first resolved to their Discord IDs, and those IDs are then scanned. Resolution walks a chain of verification services - RoWifi, then RoVer, then Bloxlink - and the first one that returns a link wins. Only Discord accounts whose owner gave reverse-search consent to one of those services can be matched, so an empty result is normal.

A user is reported as unflagged only when every service in the chain confirmed there is no link. If any of them is unreachable the lookup fails closed rather than guessing, so an error here means unknown, not clean.

Any server TASE detected the account in is reported as `flagType` 1 (Flagged), with the server names, detection types and activity score in the reasons and badges. A user TASE knows nothing about is returned as `flagType` 0 (Unflagged), as is a user with no consented Discord link. The content category is inferred from the reported detection types and omitted when nothing matches.

get.description:
Looks up The All Seeing Eye (TASE) records for one Roblox user, in the v2 response shape.

Resolution is identical to v1: the Roblox user ID is resolved to consented Discord IDs through RoWifi, then RoVer, then Bloxlink, and those IDs are scanned against TASE. A user is reported as unflagged only when every service in the chain confirmed there is no link; if any is unreachable the lookup fails closed rather than guessing, so an error here means unknown, not clean.

Every field v1 returns is still returned, so a client that ignores `detections` renders this identically. On top of that:

- `detections` breaks the findings out per Discord account. Every linked account appears as a key, including one TASE scanned and found nothing in, whose `detectedGuilds` is then empty. An account absent from the map entirely was never scanned.
- Each entry of `detectedGuilds` carries its own `firstSeenAt` and `lastSeenAt` for date display, plus `flag_type`: `unsafe` when the sighting is undated or under a year old, `past_offender` when its newest activity, or the detection itself where no update date is reported, is a year or more old.
- `firstSeenAt` and `lastSeenAt` on the record itself span every detection in it. These are detection dates and are independent of `lastUpdated`, which is when the record was produced.
- `flagType` rolls up the severest server grading, so a record made entirely of historical sightings comes back as `flagType` 6 (Past offender) rather than as a live confirmation.

Nullable fields are omitted rather than sent as null, so a missing `firstSeenAt` means TASE reported no detection date, not the epoch.
